chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from some of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Ali (peace be upon him) to Yemen. When he arrived, he said to him, 'Tell me of the most surprising thing that has come to you.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, a group of men came to me who had purchased a slave girl, and they all had intercourse with her in one period of purity, so she gave birth to a boy. They all disputed over him, each claiming him. So I cast lots among them and gave him to the one whose lot was drawn, and I guaranteed his share to the others.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Among a group who dispute and then entrust their matter to Allah, the lot will always come out for the one who is right.'

key_terms.الْمُحِقِّ: The one who is right/true; referring to the person who is actually entitled to the claim.
key_terms.جَارِيَة: Slave girl; a female servant or concubine in the context of classical Islamic law.
key_terms.طُهْر: Period of purity; the time between menstrual periods during which intercourse is permissible.
key_terms.فَوَّضُوا أَمْرَهُمْ إِلَى اللَّهِ: Entrusted their matter to Allah; a phrase indicating reliance on divine will through a mechanism like casting lots.
key_terms.قُرْعَة: Casting lots; a method of random selection used in Islamic jurisprudence to resolve disputes or distribute shares.

ai.seo_question: How did Ali (peace be upon him) resolve a paternity dispute among multiple men who had intercourse with the same slave girl?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in the chapter on conflicting evidence, illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *qur'ah* (casting lots) as a valid mechanism for resolving paternity disputes when clear evidence is absent. The Prophet’s affirmation that the lot favors the 'one who is truly right' (*al-muhiqq*) underscores the belief that divine selection reveals truth in matters of uncertainty, a concept deeply rooted in Shia legal theory regarding the resolution of ambiguous claims.
